title: Indian Markets Open Flat as Fed Holds Rates and FII Selling Extends to Third Session
excerpt: Sensex and Nifty trade cautiously amid mixed global cues, with IT stocks showing strength while consumer durables and realty drag.
body:
• Sensex traded near 77,655 and Nifty around 24,280 on July 30, with both indices showing marginal gains after opening flat
  • The US Federal Reserve held interest rates at 3.75% on Wednesday, matching market expectations, though forward guidance signalled caution
  • FIIs continued as net sellers for a third consecutive session, with DIIs providing buying support worth over ₹5,400 crore
  • IT stocks led gains with Nifty IT up 1.8%, while Nifty Realty dropped 1.3% as the weakest sector of the day

Markets Tread Water After Fed Decision

Indian benchmark indices opened flat on Thursday, July 30, as traders digested the US Federal Reserve's decision to hold interest rates steady at 3.75% — its fourth consecutive pause. The Nifty 50 traded around 24,280, up 0.1%, while the Sensex hovered near 77,655 after gaining 889 points in the previous session.

The cautious open extended what has been a choppy week for Indian equities. In the three sessions leading into Thursday, the Sensex had slipped 0.83% and the Nifty had declined 0.87%, weighed down by persistent foreign institutional investor (FII) selling and the absence of progress on a US-India trade deal.

Fed Holds, but Forward Guidance Splits Markets

The Federal Reserve's rate decision landed squarely on expectations, but the accompanying statement hinted at possible rate adjustments later in 2026. Markets are now watching Thursday's US Core PCE Price Index — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge — with forecasts pointing to a 0.1% month-over-month reading, sharply lower than May's 0.3%.

A softer-than-expected PCE print could reinforce rate-cut expectations for later this year, which would typically benefit emerging market flows. But for now, the signal remains mixed.

"Two factors which were weighing on Indian markets — the crude price hike and sustained FPI selling — are now behind us and have reversed."

— VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments

Sectoral Divergence Defines the Session

The day's trading showed clear sectoral splits. Nifty IT led the charge, rising 1.8%, with Wipro up 2.7% and tech stocks broadly benefiting from the weaker dollar and stable US rate outlook. Nifty Auto gained 1.1%.

On the flip side, Nifty Realty fell 1.3% and Nifty Chemicals dropped 0.7%. Among Nifty 50 stocks, Adani Ports fell 2.5% and Asian Paints declined 1.5%, emerging as the session's biggest drags. ONGC was among the top gainers, up 2.3%.

The advance-decline ratio stood at 31:19 in favour of advancers, suggesting positive breadth beneath the headline numbers.

FII Outflows Persist, but the Rupee Holds

Foreign institutional investors remained net sellers, continuing a trend that has seen ₹3,893 crore in equity outflows on July 24 alone. Domestic institutional investors, however, have consistently absorbed the selling pressure, with net purchases of ₹5,453 crore on the same day.

The rupee held relatively steady, trading around 90.39 against the US dollar, supported by lower crude oil prices. Brent crude hovered near $78 per barrel, well below the levels that had pressured Indian markets earlier this year.

Key Data Points to Watch

Beyond the US PCE data due later Thursday, markets are watching the Bank of England's rate decision (expected hold at 3.75%) and Friday's Bank of Japan decision. India's 10-year bond yield stood at 6.59%, while gold futures traded near ₹141,813 and silver at ₹217,725.

With the earnings season delivering mixed signals — L&T profit rose 14% but Air India losses ballooned — stock-specific moves are likely to dominate until clearer macro direction emerges from the week's remaining central bank decisions.
